definitions.explanation: A situation where progress has completely stopped and neither side can advance. Used for negotiations, conflicts, competitions, and other situations where opposing forces are locked in place.

examples.japanese: {交渉|こうしょう}が{膠着|こうちゃく}{状態|じょうたい}に{陥|おちい}った。
examples.english: The negotiations fell into a deadlock.

examples.japanese: {試合|しあい}は{膠着|こうちゃく}したまま{後半|こうはん}に{入|はい}った。
examples.english: The game entered the second half still in a stalemate.

examples.japanese: {与野党|よやとう}の{対立|たいりつ}で{国会|こっかい}{審議|しんぎ}が{膠着|こうちゃく}し、{重要|じゅうよう}{法案|ほうあん}の{成立|せいりつ}が{見通|みとお}せない{状況|じょうきょう}だ。
examples.english: Due to the conflict between the ruling and opposition parties, parliamentary deliberations have deadlocked, and there is no prospect of passing important legislation.

notes:
WRITING:
{膠|こう} means "glue" (from animal hides), so the word literally evokes the image of things being stuck together and unable to move.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {膠着|こうちゃく}{状態|じょうたい} (state of deadlock/stalemate)
- {膠着|こうちゃく}に{陥|おちい}る (fall into a stalemate)
- {膠着|こうちゃく}を{打破|だは}する (break a deadlock)
- {膠着|こうちゃく}した{戦線|せんせん} (stalled front line)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {行|い}き{詰|づ}まり: deadlock, impasse (more everyday)
- {停滞|ていたい}: stagnation (emphasizes lack of progress; can be one-sided)
